title: Surface Area of Solids
short: Find surface areas of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres.
trouble: Students use the height instead of the slant height for the lateral area of a cone or pyramid.

blocks.html: Surface area is the total area of a solid's outside, the paint it would take to cover it. Unfold the solid into a flat net, as in Area and Surface Area Problems, and add the areas of the pieces. The height and slant height from Volume of Pyramids, Cones and Spheres play different roles here.

Cylinder: two circles plus a rectangle whose length is the circumference, $2\pi r$, so $S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh$. Cone: the curved part unrolls into a sector of a circle with radius $\ell$ (the slant height) and arc length $2\pi r$. Its area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot \ell \cdot 2\pi r = \pi r \ell$, like the "half the apothem times the perimeter" idea. So $S = \pi r^2 + \pi r \ell$. Pyramid: the base plus triangles whose heights are the slant height $\ell$. Sphere: $S = 4\pi r^2$, exactly four times the area of a great circle (Archimedes showed this; a full proof needs calculus).

head: Solid
Surface area
rows: square pyramid, base edge $s$, slant height $\ell$
blocks.cap: Surface area formulas. $\ell$ is the slant height, measured along the face.

blocks.html: Surface area adds the areas of every face. The slanted faces of pyramids and cones use the slant height $\ell$, not the height $h$; they are related by the Pythagorean theorem.

blocks.title: A cylinder
blocks.q: Find the surface area of a cylinder with radius $3$ and height $8$.

blocks.title: A pyramid from its height
blocks.q: A square pyramid has base edge $10$ and height $12$. Find its surface area.
steps: The slant height is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $12$ (the height) and $5$ (half the base edge): $\ell = \sqrt{144 + 25} = 13$.

blocks.title: A cone
blocks.q: A cone has radius $6$ and height $8$. Find its surface area.

blocks.html: Using the height instead of the slant height for the lateral area of a cone or pyramid. The triangles and the cone's curved surface slope, so their "height" is the slant height. Check: the slant height is longer than the height, so the correct lateral area is the larger one.
